reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the Bradley-Terry model lies in its log-odds formulation, where the probability of team i beating team j is defined as π_i / (π_i + π_j), with π_i = exp(λ_i). In the time-varying case (TVC), feature weights γ_k(m_it) are allowed to vary linearly with the number of matches played, m_it. This allows for dynamic adaptation of team strength based on recent performance rather than static priors. The hierarchical Poisson log-linear (HPL) model extends this by modeling goal counts as a function of attack and defense parameters, incorporating seasonality and AR(1) structures for temporal dependencies. These two primitives together provide a complete framework for both outcome prediction and goal-scoring dynamics. The walk-forward validation ensures that models generalize well over time, avoiding overfitting to historical data. The failure mode occurs when feature weights do not adequately reflect true underlying dynamics or when temporal assumptions break down due to sudden shifts in team composition or strategy.
